Rules.title: How to play
Rules.subtitle: Everything you need to solve a crossword or a scanword here — on a phone, a tablet or a computer.

sections.title: Choosing a word
paragraphs: Tap or click any white cell. The word it belongs to lights up in yellow, and its clue appears in the bar above the grid.
Where two words cross, tap the same cell again to switch between Across and Down. In a scanword you can also tap the clue cell itself.

sections.title: Typing
paragraphs: On a computer, just type — no need to switch your keyboard layout: if your keyboard is set to English, the keys type the letters of the puzzle's language in their usual places.
On a phone or tablet, the puzzle's own keyboard appears below the grid. For Armenian it has the single letters ՈՒ and և, each filling one cell; typing ո then ւ joins them into ՈՒ automatically.
In Russian puzzles the letter Ё is written as Е, as in printed crosswords.

sections.title: Moving around
paragraphs: Arrow keys move between cells; an arrow across the current direction first turns the cursor. Enter jumps to the next clue, Shift+Enter to the previous one.
Backspace clears a letter and steps back. Home and End jump to the start and end of the word. Tab leaves the grid.

sections.title: Getting help
paragraphs: Check marks wrong letters with a red strike-through and locks the right ones. Reveal fills in a letter, a word or the whole puzzle; revealed letters carry a small purple flag.
Turn on “Check as I type” in the settings if you'd like instant feedback.

sections.title: Fresh words, every time
paragraphs: Your device remembers the words it has shown you and never asks for them again. Every new puzzle is made of words you haven't met here yet.

Faq.title: Questions and answers
Faq.subtitle: Everything about Crossword AI in one place: the puzzles, how the AI writes them, playing on any device, and your privacy.

items.question: What is Crossword AI?
items.answer: Crossword AI is a website that generates crosswords and scanwords in thirty-three languages. An AI model writes the words and clues natively in each language, code builds the grid, and each device only gets words it hasn't seen before.

items.question: Is Crossword AI free?
items.answer: Partly. Every month you get 11 free credits — enough for a medium puzzle — with no sign-up, and signing in adds 11 more each month. Free credits don't carry over to the next month. Beyond that, puzzles are paid with credits you buy: a pack is bought once — there's no subscription, bought credits never expire, and there are no ads. Playing a puzzle someone shared with you is always free.

items.question: Do I need an account?
items.answer: Not for your 11 free credits a month: your progress, your settings and the words you've already seen are kept in your browser. An account adds 11 more free credits every month and lets you buy credits and keep them.

items.question: How much does a puzzle cost?
items.answer: A small puzzle costs 5 credits, a medium one 10 and a large one 15; medium difficulty adds 1 credit and hard adds 2. Your 11 free credits a month cover a medium puzzle at medium difficulty. Credits come in packs of 200 for $4.99, 600 for $11.99 and 2,000 for $29.99. The checkout shows the price in your currency, with tax where it applies.

items.question: Who makes Crossword AI?
items.answer: It is an independent project by developer Michael Navasardyan: puzzles that read as if a local author wrote them, in each language the site offers — Armenian, Russian and English among them.

items.question: What is the difference between a crossword and a scanword?
items.answer: A crossword lists numbered clues beside the grid, Across and Down. A scanword prints each clue inside a grid cell, with an arrow pointing to where its answer goes — the format puzzle magazines across Russia and Armenia are full of.

items.question: How big are the puzzles?
items.answer: There are three sizes. A classic crossword fills a 9×9, 13×13 or 15×15 grid with roughly 8–14, 16–24 or 22–34 words, then is cropped to the words it holds. A scanword uses an 8×10, 10×13 or 13×17 grid — taller than it is wide, because most are solved on a phone.

items.question: How do the difficulty levels differ?
items.answer: Easy uses everyday words with direct definitions. Medium draws on a broader vocabulary. Hard brings rarer words and clues that make you think twice.

items.question: Which topics can I choose?
items.answer: Twelve: everyday words, nature, animals, food & drink, geography, history, science, sport, arts, home & everyday, professions and local culture — or mix them all in one puzzle.

items.question: Will I ever see the same word twice?
items.answer: Not on the same device. It remembers up to 4,000 words per language — about 130 puzzles' worth — and leaves them out of every new puzzle; only after that do the oldest drop off the list. Clearing your browser's site data starts the list over.

items.question: How does the AI write the clues?
items.answer: Google's Gemini model writes words and clues directly in each language, following a style guide by native speakers. Code then checks every one — the right alphabet, one real word, a fair clue that doesn't give the answer away — and a second AI pass acts as an editor. Anything that fails is dropped, never patched. The grid itself is built by code, not by the AI.

items.question: What if a clue is wrong?
items.answer: Open the ⋯ menu above the grid and choose “Report a clue”. Once three different players report the same clue, it is retired and never appears again.

items.question: How do I type answers on a phone or a computer?
items.answer: On a computer, just type: even if your keyboard is set to English, the keys type the puzzle's letters in their usual places, so there is no layout to switch. On a phone or tablet, the puzzle's own keyboard appears below the grid, and the system keyboard never covers it.

items.question: Can I check my answers or get a hint?
items.answer: Yes. Check marks wrong letters in one cell, one word or the whole puzzle, and Reveal fills in a letter, a word or everything. Turn on “Check as I type” in the settings to see mistakes the moment you make them.

items.question: How are Armenian ու and և, and Russian Ё, handled?
items.answer: In Armenian puzzles ու and և are single letters and each fills one cell, as in printed Armenian crosswords; the on-screen keyboard has both, and typing ո then ւ joins them into ու. In Russian puzzles Ё is written as Е, as in printed crosswords.

items.question: Is my progress saved?
items.answer: Yes, automatically, as you play. Every crossword or scanword you start and leave unfinished is listed under “My puzzles”, with your letters saved, so you can continue any of them later — even offline.

items.question: Can I play offline, or install it as an app?
items.answer: Yes. Crossword AI installs from your browser like an app (on iPhone: Share → Add to Home Screen). Every puzzle you open is saved with your progress and keeps working without a connection; only new puzzles need the internet.

items.question: Can I share a puzzle with a friend?
items.answer: Yes. Tap Share above the grid to copy the link, or send it through WhatsApp, Telegram, Facebook, X, VK or email. Your friend gets exactly the same grid and clues.

items.question: Can I play with a keyboard or a screen reader?
items.answer: Yes. The grid works fully from the keyboard and with screen readers: every cell is labeled, the active clue is announced, and checks and reveals are read out. Wrong and revealed letters are marked by shape, never by color alone.

items.question: What data do you keep?
items.answer: Very little. Your puzzles, progress, settings and seen-word list stay in your browser. The server stores the puzzles that are created (so a shared link opens the same grid), clue reports with a one-way hash of the IP address, and anonymous solve counts. No names and no profiles.

items.question: Is anything about me sent to the AI?
items.answer: No. Only puzzle settings — language, topic, difficulty — and lists of words go to Google's Gemini models, never anything about you.

About.title: About Crossword AI
About.subtitle: A puzzle generator that writes in your language and never serves the same word twice.

sections.title: Why we made it
paragraphs: Most online crosswords recycle a small word list, and most translated ones read like translations. We wanted puzzles that feel written by a local author — and that stay new no matter how many you solve.

sections.title: How the words are written
paragraphs: An AI model writes words and clues directly in each language, following a style guide by native speakers: the grammatical forms crosswords use, the spelling norm, the way clues are phrased in that language's puzzle tradition.

Every word then passes automatic checks — the right alphabet, one real word, no clue that gives the answer away — and a second AI acting as an editor. Players' reports retire anything that slips through.

sections.title: How the grids are built
paragraphs: The grid itself is built by code, not by the AI: an algorithm fits the words together so every letter belongs to a real word with a clue. That is what keeps every puzzle fair.

Privacy.title: Privacy policy
Privacy.subtitle: Short version: an account only if you want one, no profiling. Here is everything we keep.

sections.title: On your device
paragraphs: Your browser stores the puzzles you open, your progress, your settings and a list of the words you have already seen, so they are never repeated. This stays on your device; clearing site data removes it.

sections.title: On our server
paragraphs: We store the puzzles that are created, so a shared link opens the same grid. When you report a clue we keep the report with a one-way hash of your IP address, only so that one person cannot retire a clue alone. We also count anonymously how puzzles are played (solved, which words were revealed) to tune difficulty.

To give each device its free credits of the month, the site sets a cookie holding a random identifier. With each puzzle paid with free credits we keep that identifier and a one-way hash of your IP address.

sections.title: Accounts and credits
paragraphs: If you create an account, we keep your name, your email address and, when you sign in with Google, your Google profile picture. We also keep your credit balance and its history: each purchase, each puzzle paid for and each refund.

sections.title: Payments
paragraphs: Payments are processed by Paddle.com, our Merchant of Record. Paddle collects your payment details and billing country under its own privacy policy; we never see your card number. From Paddle we receive the amount, currency, tax and payment method type of each purchase.

sections.title: AI provider
paragraphs: New words and clues are written by Google's Gemini models. Only the puzzle settings (language, topic, difficulty) and lists of words are sent — never anything about you.

sections.title: Analytics and error reports
paragraphs: With your consent, Google Analytics counts page views and sets its cookies to tell visits apart; without it, analytics runs without cookies. You can change your answer at any time under "Cookie settings" at the bottom of every page. Sentry receives error reports with no personal details. Neither is used for ads or profiling.
Pages in some languages load their font from Google Fonts, which receives your IP address with that request.

Terms.title: Terms of use
Terms.subtitle: Crossword AI is for fun and learning. These terms cover playing it and buying credits.

sections.title: Using the service
paragraphs: You may play, share and print the puzzles for personal and educational use. Please don't overload the service with automated requests.

sections.title: Free and bought credits
paragraphs: Each device gets 11 free credits every calendar month, and each account 11 more. Free credits are spent before bought ones and do not carry over to the next month. Puzzles are paid with credits, at the price shown before you create one; a puzzle is charged only when it is built, and opening a stored puzzle is free.
Credits are bought in packs with a one-time payment — there is no subscription — and bought credits never expire. Credits have no cash value and cannot be transferred.

sections.title: Payments
paragraphs: Our order process is conducted by our online reseller Paddle.com. Paddle.com is the Merchant of Record for all our orders. Paddle provides all customer service inquiries and handles returns.

sections.title: Refunds
paragraphs: You can ask for a refund of a credit pack within 14 days of buying it, through Paddle or by writing to us. A refund takes the pack's credits back from your balance. Credits already spent cannot be returned, so a pack that has been partly used may be refunded in part.

sections.title: AI-written content
paragraphs: Words and clues are written by AI and checked automatically, but mistakes can happen. If you find one, report it — that's how bad clues are removed.

sections.title: No warranty
paragraphs: The service is provided as is, without guarantees of availability or accuracy. We may change or discontinue features at any time.
